answer: A scripted farm thus has to pad 125 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is recorded against the wharf challenge, the jade audit can replay the cipher history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 97 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
